title: API gateway quota enforcement — intermittent global throttling and burst amplification
creator: Asha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the March 10th quota enforcement incident where short-lived bursts bypassed expected per-customer throttles leading to elevated 429 rates and downstream capacity pressure. This ticket tracks the root cause fixes, test coverage additions, playbook updates, and an operational rollout plan to avoid recurrence.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-10T15:04Z we observed a rapid increase in 429 responses from the public API gateway for multiple customers. Traffic analysis showed repeated short-lived connection bursts that exceeded configured token-bucket quotas without being correctly accounted across gateway replicas, causing transient cascade failures and worker saturation in the routing layer.
root_cause: Race condition between local token-bucket refresh and inter-node quota reconciliation combined with a feature-flagged optimization that bypassed reconciliation for low-latency paths. Under bursty client behavior the local buckets temporarily over-issued tokens before global state converged, producing amplified request rates and 429 storms downstream.
impact: Erroneous 429s for ~12% of requests from a subset of customers for a 22-minute window; increased error budgets for several routes; a small number of customer jobs retried aggressively, increasing load and slightly raising costs for Dedicated customers.
timeline_highlights: 2026-03-10 15:02 UTC — First alert from latency/5xx dashboard (Datadog) showing spike on api-gateway-prod-01/02/03
2026-03-10 15:04 UTC — Pager duty triggered; mitigation: temporarily enabled per-node conservative throttle enforcement (manual rollback of the micro-optimization feature flag)
2026-03-10 15:26 UTC — Traffic returned to baseline after flag rollback and emergency autoscale on routing tier
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC — Post-incident war room; began RCA; captured logs and flame graphs; reproduced locally with load generator in staging
2026-03-12 14:30 UTC — Confirmed race in token refresh path; authored minimal patch to add atomic reconciliation step
2026-03-13 09:20 UTC — Integration tests added; canary deploy in us-west-2; monitored for 24 hours before broader rollout
replication_steps: Run load generator against gateway cluster with interleaved short-bursts (100ms bursts every 2s) for 10+ replicas
Enable the micro-optimization feature flag that skips reconciliation for low-latency paths
Observe local token buckets overflowing and downstream services seeing spike in requests and 429s
Collect /metrics, /debug/token-buckets and inter-node reconciliation logs to confirm timing windows
mitigations_taken: Immediate: Rolled back micro-optimization feature flag at 2026-03-10 15:04 UTC
Short-term: Emergency autoscale of routing pool and increased per-route throttling thresholds to prevent worker saturation
Medium-term: Deployed atomic reconciliation patch to gate token issuance on last-seen global state

Add synthetic burst tests to SLO evaluation that check for <1% 429s under bursty client patterns

communication_and_followup: 03/11 — Sent interim incident email to affected customers with mitigation summary
03/13 — Internal postmortem draft reviewed by Runtime and SRE leads; scheduled for exec readout 03/18
03/20 — Planned customer-facing postmortem and billing reconciliation notification
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests that reproduce the previous failure mode pass reliably in CI
Canary metrics show quota-delta < 1% and 429 rates within baseline for 48h before full rollout
Playbook and runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams
notes: This incident highlighted a gap between our low-latency optimization guardrails and operational testing. Feature flag rollouts must include synthetic fault injection for state convergence issues.

Consider longer-term work to provide a globally consistent token-bucket using a leader-based coordinator or lightweight consensus for critical quota boundaries. That work should be scoped as a follow-on project if A1/A4 do not fully mitigate.
Customer success should prepare templates for rapid communication when throttling incidents affect billing-sensitive workloads.
